title: Nuevo Laredo marks Día de Muertos today: Catrina festival at 5 p.m., 600 marigolds in bloom

content:
Nuevo Laredo marks Día de Muertos today, Sunday, November 1, with its Festival de la Catrina 2026 starting at 5 p.m. on the explanada de la Independencia, alongside public spaces newly dressed in marigolds for the holiday.

The festival's main attractions are its Catrina and Altares de Muertos contests, organized by the municipal government through its Tourism Department. The Catrina contest has two categories: children ages 1 to 12, and an open category for ages 13 and up. Prizes in the open category are 10,000 pesos for first place, 7,000 for second and 5,000 for third, plus a special prize, according to municipal announcements reported by local outlets.

The Altares de Muertos contest is open to residents, groups, organizations and public and private schools, with each altar accompanied by an explanation of its meaning and traditional elements. Prizes are 6,000 pesos for first place, 4,000 for second and 2,000 for third.

For the holiday, the city, through its Primary Public Services Department, decorated Plaza Primero de Mayo with 600 pieces of cempasúchil marigold, one of the season's most representative flowers, and decorated the heart of the Municipal Presidency building with autumn elements so residents and visitors can walk through and take photos, local reporting on November 1 said.

The celebrations follow a Día de Muertos night at the Nuevo Laredo zoo, where hundreds of families gathered in costumes for photo spaces, Day of the Dead activities, a traditional altar and film screenings in a family setting, according to November 1 local reporting.

The festival aims to keep Mexican traditions alive through art, costumes and ofrendas honoring those who are no longer here, the city said. Admission details beyond the time and place were not specified in the announcements reviewed; families planning to attend should check the city's announcements before heading out.
